title: The host daemon reports what its machine offers, and loopctl places work by those reports

story.i_want_to: see each machine's toolchains, databases, free session and CI slots and measured load, and place only where the repo can build and there is room
story.so_that: 'dev box' and 'CI host' become capacity rather than fixed roles, and a session never lands on a machine that cannot run the repo or is already saturated

rationale: PRD R3: one host daemon per machine 'reports what the machine offers: CPU, Elixir and OTP versions, databases, free CI and session slots, and measured load ... loopctl places and moves work by the daemons' reports'. The runner already sends cores, memory_mb, repos and max_sessions on join and a load sample on status (RunnerJoin, lib/loopctl/api_spec/runner_contract.ex:810; RunnerSample :675), but placement reads none of the measurements: Selection.runners/3 orders by in_flight then id (lib/loopctl/runners/selection.ex:42-56) and the sample is only echoed on the pool read (runner_controller.ex:532). The runner process becomes the host daemon by growing this report, not by a new process.

acceptance_criteria.description: Runner contract 1.40.0 (after US-52.44's 1.39.0): RunnerJoin and RunnerStatus may carry host {toolchains: {erlang: [version], elixir: [version]}, databases: [{engine: postgres | redis, version, reachable}], session_slots: {total, free}, ci_slots: {total, free, busy} | null, repos_ready: [owner/repo]}, bounded to 20 versions per toolchain, 8 databases and 50 repos; a join or status without host is accepted exactly as on the previous version.

runner/'s LoopctlRunner.HostReport.collect/1 lists toolchains from the installs directories under ASDF_DATA_DIR (default ~/.asdf), probes each database URL in the daemon config with a connect and version query bounded at 2 s, and puts in repos_ready each served repo whose checkout's .tool-versions names an installed erlang and elixir; it truncates every list to the contract's bounds.

The daemon sends host on join and on every status tick; collection runs in a task with a 5 s overall timeout, and a timed-out or crashed collection sends the status without host rather than delaying or skipping it.
RunnerChannel stores the latest host in the runner's Presence meta beside sample, and GET /api/v1/runners/pool (MCP runner_pool) returns it per runner with the age of the report.
Selection.runners/3 drops a runner whose host report lists repos_ready without the dispatch's repo; a runner that sent no host report is judged by today's repos declaration alone.

Selection.runners/3 drops a runner whose sample is older than twice the status interval or whose loadavg_1m divided by cores exceeds PLACEMENT_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE (default 1.0), and orders the rest by load per core, then in_flight, then id.

A status whose host breaks the contract's bounds is refused invalid_payload and the previous report stays in the meta; a join whose host breaks them is accepted with host dropped and a warning logged naming the runner, so a bad report never refuses the join.
runner_pool's description names the host fields and the placement rules, and deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md has a row for PLACEMENT_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE with its default and what a wrong value does.

test_cases.name: contract shape, bounds and the previous version (unit)
expected_results: host kept; accepted; invalid_payload; joined with host dropped

test_cases.name: HostReport.collect on a fixture machine (runner unit)
preconditions: temp ASDF_DATA_DIR with erlang 27.2 and elixir 1.18.1; checkouts A (.tool-versions erlang 27.2, elixir 1.18.1) and B (elixir 1.19.0); a local TCP listener answering as postgres and a closed port for redis
expected_results: toolchains listed; repos_ready [A]; postgres reachable with its version; redis reachable false within 2 s

test_cases.name: a hung probe never delays the status (runner unit)
preconditions: Control harness with a fake socket; a database probe stubbed to sleep 30 s
expected_results: status pushed within 6 s without host

test_cases.name: host reaches the pool read (channel test + ConnCase)
expected_results: the runner's entry carries host and report_age_seconds

test_cases.name: placement by readiness and load (DataCase)
preconditions: four connected runners with free slots: r1 ready, load 0.2/core; r2 ready, load 1.5/core; r3 repos_ready without the repo; r4 no host report, load 0.5/core; r5 ready with a sample 3 intervals old; a second tenant with a ready idle runner
expected_results: [r1, r4] in that order; no runner of the second tenant

test_cases.name: tool description and env doc (node --test + mix loopctl.check_env_docs)

technical_notes: Contract: RunnerJoin (runner_contract.ex:810, required list :849-858 unchanged), RunnerStatus (:1050-1068), RunnerSample (:675); the version is 1.40.0, after US-52.44's 1.39.0, which is why this story depends on US-52.44: two lanes never claim one version. A previous-version runner is accepted for one release, as PRD R7 requires of every client.

Server: RunnerChannel.handle_in/3 (lib/loopctl_web/runner_channel.ex:335) for status, join/3 (:155) and :after_join (:209) for the join's meta; Presence meta replication (lib/loopctl/runners/presence.ex) is why every list has a size bound, as RunnerJoin's own bounds explain (:818-842). Pool read: RunnerController (runner_controller.ex:266,532).

Placement: Selection.runners/3 and accepting_ids/3 (selection.ex:42,65) are the one selection DispatchDriver and TriageDispatcher share (dispatch_driver.ex:182 via Loopctl.Agents.Dispatcher.runners/3, dispatcher.ex:329); the readiness and load filters go in accepting_ids/3, which already reads the meta in memory, and the order in the query's order_by.

Runner (today /home/mkreyman/workspace/loopctl-runner, runner/ after release 2): LoopctlRunner.Health.capacity/0 and sample/2 (lib/loopctl_runner/health.ex:18,33) are the model for HostReport; Control.join_payload/4 and status_payload/3 (control.ex:436,479) add host; the status timer is handle_info(:status, ...) (control.ex:969). Database URLs and ASDF_DATA_DIR come from the daemon's config file (LoopctlRunner.Config).
ci_slots is null until US-52.48 fills it; session_slots is max_sessions minus the runner's own in-flight count, the numbers it already declares.

The load sample is per machine, so CI jobs and interactive sessions on the same box count against session placement; that is how a busy CI host stops taking sessions without a fixed role (infra decision 0021 measured exactly this on beelink).
non_goals: Running and reporting the GitHub Actions pool: US-52.48.
Placing CI jobs: GitHub Actions stays the trigger (PRD R8); the pool admits its own jobs by load.
Delivering messages to idle sessions: release 4's host-daemon duty.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.47.6: a daemon cut off from loopctl stops sending samples, its sample ages past twice the status interval, and placement skips it; Presence drops the entry when the socket dies.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.47.4: the report lives only in the runner's Presence meta for the life of its socket and is re-sent on every join and status, so a server restart or failover loses nothing that is not re-sent within one interval.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.47.7: a refused status changes nothing and the next tick sends a fresh report; reports carry no ids because each replaces the last.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.47.3: probes are bounded at 2 s each and 5 s in all, so a slow database or disk delays nothing but its own entry.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.47.4: each daemon is reached through its own socket topic runner:<id>; the report is read from Presence on any node of the cluster.

defaults: A sample older than twice the status interval counts as no sample.
Database probe timeout 2 s; whole report 5 s.
Toolchain source: ASDF_DATA_DIR installs (asdf everywhere on this fleet).
definition_of_done: On production after the runner rollout, runner_pool shows host.toolchains and repos_ready for every connected daemon, and a sandbox item is placed on the least-loaded ready machine.
